relations.definition: Indicates that a film was created with the involvement of a studio or production company.
relations.embedding_query_text: producedBy: Indicates that a film was created with the involvement of a studio or production company.

instances: Spider-Man: Brand New Day -> Columbia Pictures
Spider-Man: Brand New Day -> Marvel Studios
Spider-Man: Brand New Day -> Pascal Pictures

candidates.label: productionCompany
candidates.comment: A production relation between a creative work (like a movie or series) and the organization responsible for its creation. Also called produced by, studio, made by, created by. Examples: "The movie 'Dune' was produced by Legendary Pictures.", "The TV series 'The Crown' was produced by Left Bank Pictures.", "The video game 'Cyberpunk 2077' was produced by CD Projekt Red."

candidates.label: producer
candidates.comment: A creative role relation between a creative work and the person or organization responsible for its production. Also called production company, executive producer, creator, maker. Examples: A movie has a producer 'Steven Spielberg'. A music album has a producer 'Universal Music Group'. A TV series has a producer 'Shonda Rhimes'. Distinct from director, who is responsible for the creative vision.

candidates.label: productionDate
candidates.comment: A production date relation between a product or vehicle and the specific date it was manufactured. Also called manufactured on, made on, creation date. Examples: "A 2023 Toyota Camry has a production date of 2022-11-15.", "A vintage car has a production date of 1965-03-01.", "A smartphone has a production date of 2024-01-20."

candidates.label: manufacturer
candidates.comment: A manufacturing relation between a product and the organization that produced it. Also called: produced by, made by, fabricated by. Examples: "Smartphone manufacturer Apple", "Automobile manufacturer Toyota", "Furniture manufacturer IKEA".

candidates.label: musicBy
candidates.comment: A composer or music group responsible for the soundtrack of a creative work. Also called soundtrack by, composer of, musical score by. Examples: "Movie X musicBy 'John Williams'", "TV Series Y musicBy 'Ramin Djawadi'", "Video Game Z musicBy 'Koji Kondo'". Distinct from composer, which is for the composer of a MusicComposition.

candidates.label: resultReview
candidates.comment: The specific review created as the outcome of a review action. Also called generated review, review outcome, produced review. Examples: `ReviewAction on Product` resultReview `Customer's Product Review`, `ReviewAction on Movie` resultReview `Critic's Movie Review`, `ReviewAction on Service` resultReview `User Service Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: creator
candidates.comment: An authorship relation between a creative work or user comment and the person or organization responsible for its creation. Also called: author, originator, producer, made by. Examples: "Novel" creator "Jane Doe", "Software" creator "Acme Corp.", "Blog Post" creator "John Smith", "User Review" creator "Anonymous User". Distinct from copyrightHolder, which is about legal ownership.

candidates.label: locationCreated
candidates.comment: A creation location relation between a creative work and the place where it was created. Also called: place of creation, origin location, created in. Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.

candidates.label: albumProductionType
candidates.comment: An album production type relation between a music album and its classification based on content type (e.g., studio, live, soundtrack). Also called album category, production style, content type. Examples: "A music album's production type is 'StudioAlbum'.", "The album's production type is 'LiveAlbum'."

candidates.label: countryOfOrigin
candidates.comment: A provenance relation between a creative work or product and its country of origin. Also called: origin country, produced in, made in. Examples: "French Wine" country of origin "France", "Japanese Anime" country of origin "Japan", "German Car" country of origin "Germany", "Hollywood Movie" country of origin "United States". Distinct from countryOfAssembly, which specifies where the product was put together.

relations.definition: Indicates that an actor appears in a film.
relations.embedding_query_text: stars: Indicates that an actor appears in a film.

instances: Spider-Man: Brand New Day -> Tom Holland
Spider-Man: No Way Home -> Tom Holland
Spider-Man: No Way Home -> Tobey Maguire
Spider-Man: No Way Home -> Andrew Garfield

candidates.label: actors
candidates.comment: An actor relation between a creative work (e.g., movie, episode, video game) and a person who performs in it. Also called performer, cast member, player. Examples: "A movie's actors include 'Brad Pitt'.", "An episode's actors include 'Jennifer Aniston'." Distinct from actor, which is the preferred and more general property that also allows PerformingGroup.

candidates.label: actor
candidates.comment: An actor relation between a creative work (e.g., movie, episode, video game) or event and a person or performing group who performs in it. Also called performer, cast member, player. Examples: "A movie's actor is 'Tom Hanks'.", "A play's actor is 'The Ensemble Theatre'.", "An episode's actor is 'Jane Doe'." Distinct from actors, which is a deprecated property for the same concept.

candidates.label: characterName
candidates.comment: A naming relation for a performance role, indicating the name of the character being played. Also called "role name", "played character", "fictional name". Examples: "Actor's performance role characterName 'Hamlet'", "Actress's performance role characterName 'Juliet'". Distinct from character, which refers to the fictional person itself, whereas characterName is the name of the character in a specific performance.

candidates.label: character
candidates.comment: A fictional role relation between a creative work and a person who is a character within it. Also called "fictional person", "role played by", "depicted character". Examples: "Novel 'Pride and Prejudice' character Elizabeth Bennet", "Movie 'Star Wars' character Luke Skywalker".

candidates.label: performerIn
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between a person and an event in which they perform or participate. Also called performs in, participates in, acts in, presents at. Examples: John Doe is a performer in 'The Annual Gala'. Jane Smith is a performer in 'The City Marathon'. An actor is a performer in 'The New Play'. Distinct from performer, which points from an event to a person.

candidates.label: performer
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and an organization or person who performs at it. Also called artist, entertainer, presenter, actor. Examples: A concert has a performer 'Taylor Swift'. A play has a performer 'Meryl Streep'. A conference has a performer 'Dr. Jane Doe'. Distinct from performerIn, which points from a person to an event.

candidates.label: performers
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and its primary performers, who can be organizations or persons. Also called main artists, headliners, principal actors, featured performers. Examples: A concert has performers 'Coldplay'. A play has performers 'The Royal Shakespeare Company'. A festival has performers 'Various Artists'. Distinct from performer, which can be any performer, not necessarily the main one.

candidates.label: reviewAspect
candidates.comment: The specific part, feature, or facet of an item that a review or rating pertains to. Also called review focus, aspect reviewed, rating dimension. Examples: `Restaurant Review` reviewAspect `"Service Quality"`, `Product Rating` reviewAspect `"Battery Life"`, `Movie Review` reviewAspect `"Acting Performance"`.

candidates.label: workPresented
candidates.comment: A presented work relation between a screening event and a movie, identifying the film shown during that event. Also called screened movie, film shown, featured film. Examples: ScreeningEvent workPresented "The Matrix", FilmFestivalEvent workPresented "Parasite", DriveInMovie workPresented "Jaws". Distinct from workFeatured, which is a general showcasing, and workPerformed, which is for live enactments.

candidates.label: directors
candidates.comment: A creative leadership relation between a clip, episode, movie, or video game and the persons who directed it. Also called: directed by, filmmakers, showrunners. Examples: "Movie" directors "Joel Coen, Ethan Coen", "TV Episode" directors "Various Directors", "Video Game" directors "Hideo Kojima, Yoji Shinkawa". Distinct from director, which is a singular property for a single director.

relations.definition: Indicates that an entity holds the second position in a ranking, following another entity.
relations.embedding_query_text: rankedSecondBehind: Indicates that an entity holds the second position in a ranking, following another entity.

instances: Spider-Man: Brand New Day opening weekend -> Avengers: Endgame

chosen_property.label: rankedSecondBehind
chosen_property.definition: Indicates that a screening event ranks the movie as second place, following another movie.
chosen_property.justification: minted property as no existing candidate fits

candidates.label: position
candidates.comment: An ordinal attribute indicating the sequential position of an item within a series or list. Also called order, rank, sequence number, index. Examples: A list item has a position of '1'. A chapter in a book has a position of 'Chapter 3'. A search result has a position of '5'.

candidates.label: isPartOfBioChemEntity
candidates.comment: A biochemical part-whole relation indicating that one biochemical entity is a component of another larger biochemical entity. Also called component of biochem entity, contained within biochem entity, element of biochem entity. Examples: A protein domain isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a larger protein'. A subunit isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a protein complex'. A specific gene sequence isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a chromosome'.

candidates.label: hasCertification
candidates.comment: A certification relation between an entity (organization, person, place, product, or service) and its associated certification. Also called holds certification, certified by, possesses certification, has accreditation. Examples: "An organization has a certification for quality management.", "A product has a certification for organic ingredients.", "A person has a certification in project management."

candidates.label: clipNumber
candidates.comment: A positional relation for a clip, indicating its order within a group of clips. Also called "clip index", "clip position", "sequence number". Examples: "Video clip clipNumber 3", "Audio clip clipNumber 'Part 1'".

candidates.label: seasonNumber
candidates.comment: The numerical or textual identifier indicating a season's position within an ordered series of seasons. Also called season index, season position, season number in series. Examples: `TV Show Season` seasonNumber `1`, `Anime Series Season` seasonNumber `"Part 2"`, `Video Game Season Pass` seasonNumber `3`.

candidates.label: ratingCount
candidates.comment: A rating count relation between an aggregate rating and the total number of individual ratings contributing to it. Also called number of ratings, total ratings. Examples: "An aggregate rating has a rating count of 150.", "A product review summary has a rating count of 500.", "A movie's average rating has a rating count of 10,000."

candidates.label: taxonRank
candidates.comment: A classification of a taxon by its taxonomic rank, often expressed as a URI from a controlled vocabulary. Also called "taxonomic level", "rank in taxonomy", "biological classification". Examples: "The taxon has taxonRank 'Family'", "The species' taxonRank is 'Species'", "This taxon is classified by taxonRank 'Genus'."

candidates.label: episodeNumber
candidates.comment: An episode number relation between an episode and the integer or text representing its position within an ordered group. Also called "episode index", "sequence number", "part number". Examples: "Episode 'The Pilot' episodeNumber '1'", "TV episode episodeNumber 'Season 3, Episode 7'", "Podcast episode episodeNumber '42'".

candidates.label: lesserOrEqual
candidates.comment: A lesser or equal ordering relation between two qualitative values, indicating that the subject value is smaller than or equal to the object value. Also called: is less than or equal to, is at most, does not exceed. Examples: "Low lesserOrEqual Medium", "Small lesserOrEqual Small", "Cold lesserOrEqual Cold". Distinct from lesser, which strictly indicates a smaller value.

candidates.label: isTierOf
candidates.comment: A membership hierarchy relation between a member program tier and the larger member program it belongs to. Also called tier within, part of program, level of program. Examples: A 'Gold' tier isTierOf 'Loyalty Program X'. A 'Premium' tier isTierOf 'Subscription Service Y'. A 'Bronze' tier isTierOf 'Rewards Program Z'.

relations.definition: Indicates the person who authored or uttered a claim.
relations.embedding_query_text: madeBy: Indicates the person who authored or uttered a claim.

instances: Kevin Feige called the debut truly phenomenal -> Kevin Feige
Tom Rothman says the film is about friendship and connection -> Tom Rothman
Amy Pascal described No Way Home as 20 years in the making -> Amy Pascal

candidates.label: spokenByCharacter
candidates.comment: An attribution relation between a quotation and the character, person, or organization to whom it is attributed within a creative work. Also called "attributed to", "quote speaker", "character says", "uttered by". Examples: "The quote is spokenByCharacter Hamlet", "The dialogue was spokenByCharacter the CEO", "This line is spokenByCharacter a fictional narrator."

candidates.label: legislationPassedBy
candidates.comment: A passing authority relation between a piece of legislation and the organization or person that originally enacted it. Also called: enacted by, made by, legislated by. Examples: "Primary Legislation legislationPassedBy Parliament", "Secondary Legislation legislationPassedBy Government", "Local Bylaw legislationPassedBy City Council". Distinct from legislationResponsible, which refers to the ministry or individual in charge of elaborating or addressing questions about the legislation.

candidates.label: reviewedBy
candidates.comment: The person or organization responsible for reviewing the content of a webpage for accuracy or completeness. Also called content reviewer, page editor, accuracy checker. Examples: `Medical Information Page` reviewedBy `Dr. Jane Doe`, `News Article` reviewedBy `Fact-Checking Organization`, `Research Paper` reviewedBy `Peer Review Board`. Distinct from `author`, which indicates who created the content, not who reviewed it.

candidates.label: claimInterpreter
candidates.comment: An interpretation relation between a claim and the organization or person who interpreted it from media content. Also called "interpreted by", "claim analyst", "fact-checker". Examples: "News claim claimInterpreter FactCheck.org", "Social media claim claimInterpreter Jane Doe".

candidates.label: creator
candidates.comment: An authorship relation between a creative work or user comment and the person or organization responsible for its creation. Also called: author, originator, producer, made by. Examples: "Novel" creator "Jane Doe", "Software" creator "Acme Corp.", "Blog Post" creator "John Smith", "User Review" creator "Anonymous User". Distinct from copyrightHolder, which is about legal ownership.

candidates.label: interpretedAsClaim
candidates.comment: A claim extraction relation between a creative work or media object and a specific assertion or statement derived from its content. Also called contains claim, implies claim, claim extracted from, claim derived from. Examples: A news article is interpretedAsClaim 'The sky is blue'. A scientific paper is interpretedAsClaim 'Drug X cures Y'. A video is interpretedAsClaim 'Candidate Z made promise A'.

candidates.label: legislationCountersignedBy
candidates.comment: A countersignature relation between a piece of legislation and the person or organization that countersigned it. Also called: countersigned by, officially endorsed by, co-signed by. Examples: "The Bill of Rights legislationCountersignedBy President Washington", "EU Directive 2023/45 legislationCountersignedBy European Commission", "Local Ordinance legislationCountersignedBy City Clerk".

candidates.label: readBy
candidates.comment: A narration relation between an audiobook and the person who performs the reading. Also called narrated by, performed by, voiced by. Examples: "The audiobook 'Harry Potter' is read by 'Stephen Fry'.", "An autobiography audiobook is read by 'the author'.", "A classic novel audiobook is read by 'a professional narrator'."

candidates.label: noBylinesPolicy
candidates.comment: A policy statement from a news media organization explaining when authors are not credited in bylines. Also called anonymous author policy, byline exclusion policy, uncredited author policy. Examples: "News Org A noBylinesPolicy 'https://news.example.com/bylines'", "Journalism Company B noBylinesPolicy 'Our policy is to omit bylines for staff editorials.'", "Media Outlet C noBylinesPolicy 'https://media.example.org/editorial-standards#bylines'".

candidates.label: publishedBy
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a publication event and the organization or person responsible for it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book's publication event was published by 'Penguin Random House'.", "A journal article's publication event was published by 'Elsevier'.", "A blog post's publication event was published by 'Jane Doe'.". Distinct from publisher, which refers to the publisher of the creative work itself.

relations.definition: Indicates that a claim concerns a particular film.
relations.embedding_query_text: aboutFilm: Indicates that a claim concerns a particular film.

instances: Kevin Feige called the debut truly phenomenal -> Spider-Man: Brand New Day
Tom Rothman says the film is about friendship and connection -> Spider-Man: Brand New Day
Amy Pascal described No Way Home as 20 years in the making -> Spider-Man: No Way Home

chosen_property.label: about
chosen_property.definition: The subject of a claim or statement concerns a particular entity or topic.

candidates.label: interpretedAsClaim
candidates.comment: A claim extraction relation between a creative work or media object and a specific assertion or statement derived from its content. Also called contains claim, implies claim, claim extracted from, claim derived from. Examples: A news article is interpretedAsClaim 'The sky is blue'. A scientific paper is interpretedAsClaim 'Drug X cures Y'. A video is interpretedAsClaim 'Candidate Z made promise A'.

candidates.label: claimReviewed
candidates.comment: A summary relation for a claim review, providing a short text of the specific claims being reviewed. Also called "reviewed claim", "claim summary", "subject of review". Examples: "Fact-check review claimReviewed 'Eating apples cures cancer'", "Product claim review claimReviewed 'This product doubles battery life'".

candidates.label: workPresented
candidates.comment: A presented work relation between a screening event and a movie, identifying the film shown during that event. Also called screened movie, film shown, featured film. Examples: ScreeningEvent workPresented "The Matrix", FilmFestivalEvent workPresented "Parasite", DriveInMovie workPresented "Jaws". Distinct from workFeatured, which is a general showcasing, and workPerformed, which is for live enactments.

candidates.label: firstAppearance
candidates.comment: A first appearance relation between a claim and the creative work where it was initially known to occur. Also called: initial publication, original mention, debut in. Examples: "Claim: Earth is flat" first appearance "Ancient Greek Texts", "Claim: COVID-19 is a hoax" first appearance "Social Media Post", "Claim: New drug cures cancer" first appearance "Unverified Online Article".

candidates.label: appearance
candidates.comment: An appearance relation between a claim and a creative work where that claim is found or occurs. Also called occurrence in, mentioned in, found in. Examples: "A claim's appearance is in 'News Article X'.", "The factual claim's appearance is in 'Research Paper Y'."

candidates.label: claimInterpreter
candidates.comment: An interpretation relation between a claim and the organization or person who interpreted it from media content. Also called "interpreted by", "claim analyst", "fact-checker". Examples: "News claim claimInterpreter FactCheck.org", "Social media claim claimInterpreter Jane Doe".

candidates.label: associatedClaimReview
candidates.comment: A claim review related to another review by common content, topic, or claim. Also called: related claim review, linked claim assessment. Examples: "Review 'MediaReview of Article' associatedClaimReview 'ClaimReview of Statement'", "Review 'FactCheck' associatedClaimReview 'Another FactCheck'". Distinct from associatedMediaReview, which links to a media review.

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: associatedMediaReview
candidates.comment: A media review related to another review by common content, topic, or claim. Also called: related media review, linked media assessment. Examples: "Review 'ClaimReview of Statement' associatedMediaReview 'MediaReview of Article'", "Review 'ProductReview' associatedMediaReview 'VideoReview'". Distinct from associatedClaimReview, which links to a claim review.

candidates.label: mentions
candidates.comment: A mention relation between a creative work and a thing it references without necessarily being about. Also called: references, alludes to, cites. Examples: "News Article mentions 'Climate Change'", "Book mentions 'Historical Event'", "Speech mentions 'Famous Person'". Distinct from about, which indicates the primary topic of the creative work.

instances: Tom Rothman -> Sony Pictures Motion Picture Group

candidates.label: hasCertification
candidates.comment: A certification relation between an entity (organization, person, place, product, or service) and its associated certification. Also called holds certification, certified by, possesses certification, has accreditation. Examples: "An organization has a certification for quality management.", "A product has a certification for organic ingredients.", "A person has a certification in project management."

candidates.label: holdingArchive
candidates.comment: A holding archive relation between an archive component and the archive organization that maintains it. Also called maintained by, kept by, archive holder. Examples: "An archive component has a holding archive 'National Archives'.", "The document is part of a holding archive.", "This record is held by a specific holding archive."

candidates.label: jobTitle
candidates.comment: An occupational role relation between a person and their formal designation within an organization. Also called position, role, occupation, professional title. Examples: A person has a jobTitle of 'Software Engineer'. A person has a jobTitle of 'Chief Executive Officer'. A person has a jobTitle of 'Marketing Manager'.

candidates.label: hasCredential
candidates.comment: A credential relation between an organization or person and an awarded credential. Also called holds credential, awarded credential, possesses credential. Examples: "A person has a credential as a licensed engineer.", "An organization has a credential for business excellence.", "The professional has a credential in data science."

candidates.label: subtitleLanguage
candidates.comment: An identification of the languages in which subtitles or captions are available for a broadcast event, movie, or TV episode. Also called "caption language", "available subtitles", "subtitle options". Examples: "The movie has subtitleLanguage English", "The TV episode's subtitleLanguage is Spanish", "This broadcast event offers subtitles in multiple subtitleLanguage options."

candidates.label: alternativeHeadline
candidates.comment: An alternative headline relation between a creative work and its secondary title. Also called subtitle, secondary title, sub-headline. Examples: "A news article's alternative headline is 'Local Hero Saves Cat'.", "A book's alternative headline is 'A Novel of Intrigue'."

candidates.label: containsPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and another smaller place that it contains. Also called "includes place", "encompasses", "holds". Examples: "Country 'France' containsPlace 'Paris'", "City 'Paris' containsPlace 'Eiffel Tower'". Distinct from containedIn or containedInPlace, which are the inverse relations.

candidates.label: caption
candidates.comment: A descriptive text or media object providing a caption for an audio, image, or video object. Also called "description", "subtitle", "alt text". Examples: "Image object caption 'Sunset over the mountains'", "Video object caption 'English subtitles'", "Audio object caption 'Transcript of speech'".

candidates.label: owns
candidates.comment: A thing that is owned by an organization or person. Also called possesses, holds title to, has ownership of. Examples: "John Doe owns 'a car'", "Acme Corp owns 'a patent'", "Sarah owns 'her house'". Distinct from memberOf, which describes membership in a group.

candidates.label: archiveHeld
candidates.comment: An archive held relation between an archive organization and a collection, fonds, or item maintained by it. Also called archival holding, collection maintained, item preserved. Examples: "The National Archives' archive held is 'Presidential Papers'.", "The historical society's archive held is 'Local Family Records'."

candidates.label: owner
candidates.comment: A person or organization that owns a thing. Also called proprietor, possessor, title holder. Examples: "Car owner 'John Doe'", "Company owner 'Acme Corp'", "House owner 'Smith Family Trust'". Distinct from creator, who made the thing.

candidates.label: ownedFrom
candidates.comment: The date and time when ownership of a product was obtained. Also called acquisition date, purchase date, date acquired. Examples: "Car OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2020-01-15'", "House OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2018-06-01T10:00:00'", "Book OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2023-03-10'". Distinct from ownedThrough, which is the date ownership ended.

candidates.label: issuedBy
candidates.comment: An issuing authority relation between a certification, permit, or ticket and the organization that granted or provided it. Also called granted by, provided by, authorized by, issuer. Examples: A driver's license is issuedBy 'Department of Motor Vehicles'. A concert ticket is issuedBy 'Ticketmaster'. A professional certification is issuedBy 'Certification Body X'.

candidates.label: owns
candidates.comment: A thing that is owned by an organization or person. Also called possesses, holds title to, has ownership of. Examples: "John Doe owns 'a car'", "Acme Corp owns 'a patent'", "Sarah owns 'her house'". Distinct from memberOf, which describes membership in a group.

candidates.label: offeredBy
candidates.comment: An organization or person making an offer. Also called provided by, seller, vendor, offered from. Examples: "Product Offer offeredBy 'Acme Corp'", "Service Offer offeredBy 'John Doe'", "Event Ticket Offer offeredBy 'Ticketmaster'". Distinct from seller, which is a more specific term for a person or organization selling something.

candidates.label: ownedThrough
candidates.comment: The date and time when ownership of a product was relinquished. Also called disposal date, date sold, ownership end date. Examples: "Car OwnershipInfo ownedThrough '2023-05-20'", "House OwnershipInfo ownedThrough '2022-11-30T16:00:00'", "Book OwnershipInfo ownedThrough '2024-01-01'". Distinct from ownedFrom, which is the date ownership began.

candidates.label: publishedBy
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a publication event and the organization or person responsible for it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book's publication event was published by 'Penguin Random House'.", "A journal article's publication event was published by 'Elsevier'.", "A blog post's publication event was published by 'Jane Doe'.". Distinct from publisher, which refers to the publisher of the creative work itself.

candidates.label: reviewedBy
candidates.comment: The person or organization responsible for reviewing the content of a webpage for accuracy or completeness. Also called content reviewer, page editor, accuracy checker. Examples: `Medical Information Page` reviewedBy `Dr. Jane Doe`, `News Article` reviewedBy `Fact-Checking Organization`, `Research Paper` reviewedBy `Peer Review Board`. Distinct from `author`, which indicates who created the content, not who reviewed it.

candidates.label: copyrightHolder
candidates.comment: A legal ownership relation between a creative work and the person or organization holding its copyright. Also called: copyright owner, rights holder, legally owned by. Examples: "The Mona Lisa" copyright holder "The Louvre Museum", "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" copyright holder "J.K. Rowling", "Microsoft Windows" copyright holder "Microsoft Corporation".

candidates.label: legislationPassedBy
candidates.comment: A passing authority relation between a piece of legislation and the organization or person that originally enacted it. Also called: enacted by, made by, legislated by. Examples: "Primary Legislation legislationPassedBy Parliament", "Secondary Legislation legislationPassedBy Government", "Local Bylaw legislationPassedBy City Council". Distinct from legislationResponsible, which refers to the ministry or individual in charge of elaborating or addressing questions about the legislation.
